description: Takes one pitch and gate pair, folds each note into a chosen voltage window, drops immediate repeats, and hands the surviving notes round a set number of polyphonic channels

params.text: Sets the bottom of the window notes are folded into, -5V to 5V
Sets the top of the window notes are folded into, -5V to 5V
Chooses what happens to a note repeating the one before it: down, the previous pitch is played instead, so repeats alternate between two remembered pitches; up, the note is dropped
Sets how many polyphonic channels the two output jacks carry, 1 to 16; each new note is given to whichever channel has been quiet longest

inputs.text: The pitch to be folded and passed on; the voltage taken is that of the channel whose gate has risen
The gate that says a note has arrived; a rise on any channel takes that channel's pitch in

outputs.text: The folded, de-duplicated pitches, one per channel
10V on a channel that is holding a note and 0V on one that is not
A one millisecond trigger each time a repeated note is thrown away, which happens only with the switch in its upper position

notes: The fold step is not an octave. It is the gap between the two window knobs rounded down to a whole number of volts, with a floor of 1V, so the default -1.5V and 1.5V move a note by 3V
Two notes count as the same when they are within a quarter tone of each other, so a pitch that drifts by less than that is treated as a repeat
Bypassing the module passes the pitch input to the pitch output and the gate input to the gate output

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
high above 0V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
